title: Market breadth: how many are participating?
subtitle: An index can look healthy while its members tell a more varied story.
takeaway: Breadth summarizes participation across a defined universe. The universe and counting rule are as important as the indicator.

sections.title: One aggregate, four very different experiences
paragraphs: The main dataset has four fictional constituents beginning at 100. A carries 60% of initial index weight, B 20%, and C/D 10% each. At the final observation A is 110, B 98, C 97, D 95. The index is positive even though three of four constituents have lost value since the start. Rather than asking which summary is correct, reproduce the weighting and count separately.

Use a fixed-initial-weight teaching index with no constituent changes, distributions, or intervening rebalance: index level is the sum of each initial weight times its rebased price. This is a transparent toy aggregation, not a reconstruction of a named exchange index. A’s gain contributes +6 percentage points; B/C/D contribute −0.4, −0.3, −0.5. The net is +4.8 points, taking 100 to 104.8.

tables.title: Final constituent states versus the common start

sections.title: The advance–decline line accumulates net participation
paragraphs: Let adv be the count of advancing issues and dec the count of declining issues. Net advances equal adv − dec. An advance–decline line adds that daily net count to the preceding cumulative value. Fidelity’s glossary describes this cumulative concept. Choose a baseline such as zero at a documented start. The absolute cumulative level then depends on that start; changes and shape are the meaningful objects of comparison.

In a fictional 100-stock universe, day one has 60 advances, 30 declines, and 10 unchanged: net +30 and cumulative +30. Day two has 35 advances, 55 declines, and 10 unchanged: net −20 and cumulative +10. Day three has 45 advances, 45 declines, and 10 unchanged: net zero and cumulative still +10. A day with equal advances and declines does not imply unchanged prices for every member or an unchanged weighted index.

The final constituent table compares each stock with the common starting point. A daily A/D count uses the immediately preceding observation instead. At session 12, A rises 109→110, B and C are unchanged at 98 and 97, and D falls 96→95: advances = 1, declines = 1, unchanged = 2, daily net zero. Do not substitute the since-start count of one winner and three losers into the daily line.

sections.title: Different breadth measures encode different questions
paragraphs: An advance/decline ratio is adv/dec when dec is nonzero. An advancing fraction might be adv/(adv + dec), excluding unchanged issues, or adv/U, where U is all eligible issues. Those fractions differ when some issues are unchanged. On day one of the 100-stock example, 60/90 ≈ 66.67% of movers advanced, while 60/100 = 60% of the full universe advanced. Never discuss a threshold without naming its denominator and edge-case treatment.

Another measure counts stocks above a chosen moving average: 100 × eligible stocks above their average / eligible stocks with sufficient history. Equality, missing history, and the lookback must be specified. New-high and new-low counts require a lookback and a definition, such as intraday extreme versus closing extreme. Each measure condenses the market in a different way; agreement is more informative when you understand exactly which classifications are agreeing.

sections.title: The universe is part of the measurement
paragraphs: Exchange-wide issues are not automatically the same population as common stocks in an equity index. A dataset may include funds, preferred shares, or other instruments. Membership changes, new listings, delistings, and securities without adequate lookback history can change the denominator. A rising above-average percentage may reflect improved prices or removal of weak members. A well-kept analysis records how eligibility changes over time.

The historical universe should be the one available at the historical date. Using only today’s constituents can erase unsuccessful former members and create an attractive account of the past. Exchange-level breadth can also react to concentrations in certain types of listings, while a specific index reflects its own weighting and eligibility. Compare like with like when using an index and a participation series to support a conclusion.

sections.title: Trace the weighted aggregate and the counts
paragraphs: At session 2, A rises from 100 to 102 while D falls to 99 and B/C stay at 100. Index = 0.6 × 102+0.2 × 100+0.1 × 100+0.1 × 99 = 101.1. There is one advance, one decline, and two unchanged, so daily net zero. A and D receive equal votes in breadth although their initial index weights differ sixfold.

By session 10, A reaches 110 while B/C/D are 97/96/95. The index is 66+19.4+9.6+9.5 = 104.5. That session has one advance and three declines, daily net −2. At session 11 the direction count flips: A declines while B/C/D advance, daily net +2, but the index falls to 104.3 because the heavier constituent’s loss outweighs the smaller gains.

These are not just unequal gains paired with a vague story about narrowness. Every stock path is supplied, each count is derived, and both plotted summaries can be reconstructed. A positive index and weak participation invite inspection of concentration, while a negative index with more advancers invites inspection of the largest weights. The underlying table resolves the apparent contradiction.

Equal weighting would give a different final aggregation: (110+98+97+95)/4 = 100. Its zero change does not mean every stock was flat. This further contrast teaches why “the market” needs a named universe and aggregation convention, even before any indicator is added.

sections.title: Write a breadth note with a fair denominator
paragraphs: At session 12, one advance, one decline, and two unchanged give advancing fraction among movers 1/(1+1) = 50%, but advancing fraction among all eligible constituents 1/4 = 25%. The daily net is zero. The since-start count instead has one gainer out of four, with net −2. All are valid measurements, but each must name its comparison period and denominator.

For the core exercise, write the counts alongside the index contribution rather than calling the index healthy or weak without evidence. A defensible final note is “the fixed-weight toy index gained 4.8% from its start, led by the 60%-weight constituent; only one of four stocks gained over that interval.” It says precisely what the data establish.

For real datasets, first inspect whether the population includes common stocks, funds, or other issues, and how new listings, delistings, unchanged prices, and insufficient histories affect the denominator. The above-average metric introduced earlier requires sufficient history for the chosen window. Those eligibility questions should precede any numerical threshold. This edition reports no study testing whether a breadth divergence — an index rising while participation narrows, or the reverse — predicts later index returns. Do not infer a forecast from this accounting example.

example.title: A positive index with three since-start decliners
example.text: Final weighted index = 0.60 × 110+0.20 × 98+0.10 × 97+0.10 × 95 = 104.8, a +4.8% move from 100. Only A rose from the initial 100, so since-start breadth is one advance and three declines, net −2. Daily session-12 net is instead zero because A rose, B/C were unchanged, and D fell from session 11. The same data answer two different period questions.

exercise: Recalculate final index 104.8 and the since-start advance/decline count. Then compute session-12 daily net and advancing fractions among movers and all eligible stocks.

quiz.question: At session 12, what fraction of daily movers advanced?
quiz.explanation: One advance among two moving constituents gives 50%.
feedback: 25% uses all four eligible constituents, including two unchanged, in the denominator.
One advance among two moving constituents gives 50%.
75% is session 11’s figure (three advances, one decline). At session 12 only A advanced, and only two constituents moved.

figures.title: Inputs behind the two summaries
figures.caption: Constituent levels are the exact data used for index and daily counts.

solution: Weighted final level is 66+19.6+9.7+9.5 = 104.8. Since start: A rises, B/C/D fall, so advances = 1, declines = 3, net −2.
From session 11 to 12, A rises, D falls, B/C are unchanged: advances = 1, declines = 1, unchanged = 2. Daily net is zero. Among movers 1/2 = 50% advanced; among all constituents 1/4 = 25%.

practice.title: Reconstruct session 2
practice.question: Use A = 102, B = 100, C = 100, D = 99. Calculate weighted index, daily net, and unchanged count from initial 100s.
solution: Index is 61.2+20+10+9.9 = 101.1. A advances, D declines, B/C unchanged; net 1−1 = 0, unchanged = 2.
The larger weight on A explains the positive aggregate; breadth gives equal directional votes.

practice.title: Three advancers while the index falls
practice.question: A fresh fictional five-stock index fixes the table’s initial weights at session 0, with no rebalance, distributions or membership changes. All rebased price levels are 100 at session 0. Calculate the session-1 weighted index and its change from 100; advances, declines and unchanged counts; advancing fractions among movers and among all five stocks. Then calculate each eligible three-session SMA through session 1 and the percentage strictly above it, excluding insufficient history and treating equality as not above. Explain why dividing by five is wrong for that last measure, and write a note separating weighted performance from participation.
solution: Compared with session 0, B/C/D advance, A declines and E is unchanged: advances 3, declines 1, unchanged 1; net advances +2. Advancing fraction among movers is 3/(3 + 1) = 75%; among all five is 3/5 = 60%. These daily counts use session 0, not session −1.

Three-session SMAs use sessions −1, 0 and 1: A (98 + 100 + 96)/3 = 98; B (103 + 100 + 103)/3 = 102; C (104 + 100 + 102)/3 = 102; D (102 + 100 + 101)/3 = 101. A is below, B above, C/D equal. E has only two observations, so its three-session SMA is undefined. One of four eligible stocks is strictly above its SMA: 25%, rather than 1/5 = 20%. Including E would silently classify unavailable information as not above.

Example note: “From session 0 to session 1, the fixed-initial-weight index fell 1.30% despite three advancers, one decliner and one unchanged stock, because A’s 55% weight dominated the aggregate. Separately, at the session-1 close one of four stocks with a complete three-session history (sessions −1 to 1) was strictly above its mean; E was excluded for insufficient history.” Equivalent wording earns credit if it names both comparison periods, the weighting, equality policy and eligibility denominator. Neither count establishes future direction.

evidence.location: Fixed-weight table; all-path figure; daily count table; solutions; fresh five-stock independent task.
evidence.summary: Computed initial-weight sums, contributions, daily/since-start classifications and denominator contrasts. Fresh index ends at 98.70 with 3 advances/1 decline/1 unchanged; 1 of 4 eligible stocks is strictly above its complete three-session SMA.
evidence.limits: The four-member main index and five-member transfer task use fictional fixed initial weights; neither reconstructs a named real index methodology.

evidence.summary: Original four-member universe, fixed initial weights, preceding 100 values, and no rebalance define the demonstration.
evidence.limits: These assumptions simplify aggregation and cannot be silently transferred to a changing real universe.
